chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام pronounced five takbirs over Sahl ibn Hunayf, and he had been among the people of Badr. Then he walked for a while, then set him down and pronounced another five takbirs over him. He continued doing that until he had pronounced twenty-five takbirs over him.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: title of Imam Ali عليه السلام
key_terms.بَدْرِيًّا: one who participated in the Battle of Badr
key_terms.تَكْبِيرَاتٍ: the ritual declarations of 'Allahu Akbar' in the funeral prayer
key_terms.خَمْسًا وَعِشْرِينَ تَكْبِيرَةً: a total of twenty-five takbirs pronounced over the deceased
key_terms.كَبَّرَ: he pronounced the takbir in the funeral prayer
key_terms.وَضَعَهُ: he set the deceased down after carrying him

ai.seo_question: Can the funeral prayer be performed over a جنازة more than once in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام performed the funeral prayer over Sahl ibn Hunayf repeatedly, pronouncing five takbirs each time until they totaled twenty-five. It indicates the permissibility of performing salat over a جنازة more than once and highlights the distinguished status of Sahl ibn Hunayf as one of the people of Badr.
